newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Germany says will not submit to Iran "blackmail".
newsitem.headline: Germany says will not submit to Iran "blackmail".

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Thursday denounced as improper Iran's refusal to accept the return of its ambassador and said his country would not submit to "blackmail".
"We will not impose our ambassadors on Tehran," Kinkel told a news conference at the close of a two-day visit to Romania. "We Germans won't let ourselves be blackmailed or divided."

Kinkel said Iranian statements that the German and Danish ambassadors were not welcome to return were motivated by a European Union decision to send envoys back to Iran but halt political dialogue. Iran's current presidential election campaign had also played a role, he said.
"That obviously led the Tehran leadership, which is now in an electoral campaign, to react in this way, which I personally see as totally improper," he said.

He suggested EU countries would not now send their ambassadors back. "European solidarity will be shown again and for that I am thankful," he said. "We will not allow Iran to continue its election campaign at our cost and we will evaluate the situation after the elections in Iran."
The EU initially withdrew its ambassadors earlier this month after a German court implicated senior Iranian officials in the 1992 killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
